raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`POST /v1/videos` on Wan-Animate-2 at `size=720x1280` with a reference image and a driving video of slightly different aspect ratios (1072x592 and 538x304) fails in the first DiT forward of the first clip, on both checkpoints:

```
RuntimeError: The expanded size of the tensor (3520) must match the existing size (3555) at non-singleton dimension 2
```

**How the inputs are sized.** The requested `size` is a pixel-area budget, not an output resolution. `resize_by_area` fits the reference image and the driving video to that area independently, each at its own aspect ratio, with both sides floored to a multiple of 16. At 720x1280 the two inputs land on different grids:

| Input | Aspect | Canvas | Latent grid | Tokens per frame |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | ---: |
| Reference image, drives the output | 1.811 | 1280x704 | 80x44 | 3520 |
| Driving video | 1.770 | 1264x720 | 79x45 | 3555 |

The video grid is one latent row taller and one column narrower, and holds 35 more tokens.

**Where it breaks.** The in-context attention lays the generated frames and the reference-video frames side by side in one sequence, with one fixed-size slot per frame. `_InContextLayout` sized every slot from the generation grid alone (3520 here), so the copy that lays each reference-video frame into its slot was asked to place 3555 tokens into 3520 positions. Which input ends up with the larger grid depends on the fractional parts the floor to 16 discards, not on which aspect ratio is larger, so other budgets fail for other input pairs (576x1024 with the same inputs: 2240 against 2268).

## Modifications

`_InContextLayout.max_tokens_per_frame` is now `max(generation tokens per frame, reference-video tokens per frame)`. Everything downstream already keys on that one value: the generation and reference K/V copies, `block_mask_fn`, `_make_score_mod` (the biased keys are still generation frame 1) and the block-mask cache key, so nothing else changes. The official implementation sizes the slot from the budget itself (`width * height // 256`, 3600 here) and so holds either grid; `max(...)` is the tighter bound and needs nothing new passed into the layout.

Three CPU unit tests: the layout slot for the measured grids, with the mirrored and equal-grid cases unchanged; a 5-token reference frame against a 4-token generation frame through `_in_context_attention`, which raises on main; and `resize_by_area` on the measured inputs at 720x1280, giving the two grids and a slot equal to the larger.

No cookbook change here: the output-resolution paragraph is reworded to describe the per-input fit in the distilled Wan-Animate-2 PR (#44085), which touches the same lines.

## Accuracy Tests

Bit-identical for every request that runs today: when the two grids agree, or the video's is the smaller, `max(...)` equals the previous value, so the layout, mask, score bias and every padded tensor are unchanged. The CI case (720x1280 image and 480x832 video at 576x1024: 2304 against 2268 tokens per frame) is in that set, so its pinned ground truth stays valid.

GPU check (one GPU, base checkpoint, 4 steps, `clip_len` 37, the 1072x592 / 538x304 pair): the 720x1280 request that fails on main with the error above completes with this change and returns 237 frames at 1280x704; the same request at the default 640x800 gives a byte-identical MP4 (same md5, per-frame PSNR inf) on main and with this change.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

     assert out.shape[0] % 16 == 0 and out.shape[1] % 16 == 0
 
 
+def test_attention_slot_covers_both_grids_when_the_inputs_round_differently():
+    # The reference image and the driving video are each fitted to the budget at their own
+    # aspect ratio (_build_request_state calls resize_by_area once per input), so their
+    # 16-aligned canvases can differ by one step per side with the floor going either
+    # way. At 720x1280 a 1072x592 image lands on 1280x704 and a 538x304 video on 1264x720:
+    # the video grid is one latent row taller and one column narrower and holds more
+    # tokens per frame (79x45 = 3555 > 80x44 = 3520). The in-context layout must size its
+    # per-frame slot for both, or the reference K/V copy overflows.
+    budget = 720 * 1280
+    clip_len = 81
+    image, _ = resize_by_area(np.zeros((592, 1072, 3), np.uint8), budget, divisor=16)
+    video_frame, _ = resize_by_area(
+        np.zeros((304, 538, 3), np.uint8), budget, divisor=16
+    )
+    assert (image.shape[1], image.shape[0]) == (1280, 704)
+    assert (video_frame.shape[1], video_frame.shape[0]) == (1264, 720)
+
+    # Generation grid: the image canvas through the VAE (//8) and the (2, 2) patch (//2);
+    # reference-video grid: the same for the video canvas, one frame fewer (no
+    # reference-image frame), as build_clip_conditioning derives it from the VAE latent.
+    full_clip_grid = generation_token_grid(
+        clip_len, image.shape[0] // 8, image.shape[1] // 8
+    )
+    reference_video_grid = (
+        full_clip_grid[0] - 1,
+        video_frame.shape[0] // 8 // 2,
+        video_frame.shape[1] // 8 // 2,
+    )
+    assert full_clip_grid == (22, 44, 80)
+    assert reference_video_grid == (21, 45, 79)
+
+    layout = _InContextLayout(full_clip_grid, reference_video_grid, full_clip_grid)
+    assert layout.generation_video_tokens_per_frame == 3520
+    assert layout.reference_video_tokens_per_frame == 3555
+    assert layout.max_tokens_per_frame == 3555
+    assert layout.max_tokens_per_frame >= layout.generation_video_tokens_per_frame
+    assert layout.max_tokens_per_frame >= layout.reference_video_tokens_per_frame
+
+
 # build_clip_conditioning: per-clip tensors from the request state with stand-in encoders.

@@ -238,6 +239,93 @@ def slot(t, i):
     assert not any(valid(qi, reference_start + ki) for qi in (0, 1) for ki in (0, 1))
 
 
+def test_attention_slots_fit_a_reference_frame_wider_than_the_generation_frame():
+    # resize_by_area fits the reference image and the driving video to the pixel budget
+    # independently, so the reference video's grid can hold more tokens per frame than the
+    # generation grid (720x1280 with 16:9-ish inputs: 79x45 against 80x44). The slot must
+    # then take the reference frame's width, or the reference K/V copy raises "The expanded
+    # size of the tensor (4) must match the existing size (5)".
+    layout = _InContextLayout((2, 2, 2), (1, 1, 5), (2, 2, 2))
+    captured = {}
+
+    def fake_flex_attention(q, k, v, *, block_mask, score_mod):
+        captured.update(q=q, k=k, v=v)
+        return torch.zeros_like(q)
+
+    batch, heads, dim = 1, 2, 8
+
+    def tokens(values, scale):
+        base = torch.tensor(values, dtype=torch.float32).view(1, len(values), 1, 1)
+        return (base * scale).expand(batch, len(values), heads, dim).clone()
+
+    # Generation frames 0 (1..4) and 1 (5..8) of 4 tokens each; one 5-token reference frame.
+    gen_ids = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8]
+    q, k, v = tokens(gen_ids, 1.0), tokens(gen_ids, 10.0), tokens(gen_ids, 100.0)
+    reference_k = tokens([1, 2, 3, 4, 5], 1000.0)
+    reference_v = tokens([1, 2, 3, 4, 5], 10000.0)
+    with patch(f"{_BLOCK}._flex_attention_compiled", side_effect=fake_flex_attention):
+        out = WanAnimate2TransformerBlock._in_context_attention(
+            SimpleNamespace(log_scale=0.0),
+            q,
+            k,
+            v,
+            reference_k,
+            reference_v,
+            "SENTINEL_BLOCK_MASK",
+            layout,
+        )
+
+    assert tuple(out.shape) == (batch, 8, heads, dim)
+    q_padded = captured["q"].transpose(1, 2)
+    k_padded = captured["k"].transpose(1, 2)
+    v_padded = captured["v"].transpose(1, 2)
+
+    def slot(t, i):
+        return t[0, i, 0, 0].item()
+
+    # Generation tokens sit at the 5-token stride, slot 4 of each frame empty.
+    assert [slot(q_padded, i) for i in range(10)] == [1, 2, 3, 4, 0, 5, 6, 7, 8, 0]
+    assert [slot(k_padded, i) for i in range(10)] == [
+        10,
+        20,
+        30,
+        40,
+        0,
+        50,
+        60,
+        70,
+        80,
+        0,
+    ]
+    assert q_padded[:, 10:].abs().sum() == 0
+    # The five reference tokens fill their slot.
+    reference_start = layout.padded_generation_video_len
+    assert [slot(k_padded, reference_start + i) for i in range(5)] == [
+        1000,
+        2000,
+        3000,
+        4000,
+        5000,
+    ]
+    assert [slot(v_padded, reference_start + i) for i in range(5)] == [
+        10000,
+        20000,
+        30000,
+        40000,
+        50000,
+    ]
+    assert k_padded[:, 10:reference_start].abs().sum() == 0
+    assert k_padded[:, reference_start + 5 :].abs().sum() == 0
+
+    # The mask routes frame-1 queries to all five reference slots and frame-0 queries to none.
+    valid = _mask_probe(layout.block_mask_fn())
+    assert all(valid(qi, reference_start + ki) for qi in range(5, 9) for ki in range(5))
+    assert not any(
+        valid(qi, reference_start + ki) for qi in range(4) for ki in range(5)
+    )
+    assert not any(valid(qi, reference_start + 5) for qi in range(5, 9))

+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "full_clip_grid, reference_video_grid, expected_tokens_per_frame",
+    [
+        # 720x1280 budget, 1072x592 image and 538x304 video: the video's canvas (1264x720)
+        # is one latent row taller and one column narrower than the image's (1280x704),
+        # 79x45 = 3555 tokens against 80x44 = 3520; the slot takes the larger.
+        ((22, 44, 80), (21, 45, 79), 3555),
+        # Mirror case, the video's grid is the smaller: the generation grid sizes the slot.
+        ((22, 45, 79), (21, 44, 80), 3555),
+        # Equal grids: unchanged.
+        ((22, 44, 80), (21, 44, 80), 3520),
+    ],
+)
+def test_layout_slot_is_the_larger_of_the_two_grids_tokens_per_frame(
+    full_clip_grid, reference_video_grid, expected_tokens_per_frame
+):
+    layout = _InContextLayout(full_clip_grid, reference_video_grid, full_clip_grid)
+    full_clip_f = full_clip_grid[0]
+    assert layout.max_tokens_per_frame == expected_tokens_per_frame
+    assert layout.max_tokens_per_frame >= layout.generation_video_tokens_per_frame
+    assert layout.max_tokens_per_frame >= layout.reference_video_tokens_per_frame
+    assert (
+        layout.max_generation_video_num_tokens
+        == full_clip_f * expected_tokens_per_frame
+    )
+    assert (
+        layout.max_reference_video_num_tokens
+        == (full_clip_f - 1) * expected_tokens_per_frame
+    )
+    assert layout.padded_generation_video_len == (
+        math.ceil(layout.max_generation_video_num_tokens / 128) * 128
+    )
+    assert layout.padded_reference_video_len == (
+        math.ceil(layout.max_reference_video_num_tokens / 128) * 128
+    )
+
